response: ["When melanoma is suspected, the whole lesion should be completely excised with a narrow (1-3 mm) margin to perform histological diagnosis.","Incisional biopsies can be performed on large lesions such as lesions on the face (e.g., lentigo maligna), acral lesions, and on the genitalia.","Surgical excision with histologically negative margins is the recommended and first-line treatment for primary cutaneous melanoma of any thickness, as well as for melanoma in situ.","Surgical margins should be based on tumor thickness.","Sentinel lymph node biopsy, when indicated, should be performed before wide excision of the primary tumor, and in the same operative setting, whenever possible.","The criteria driving the 7-point score are 'pigment_network' (atypical, 2 points), 'streaks' (irregular, 1 point), and 'dots_and_globules' (irregular, 1 point).","These three criteria are the only ones contributing to the score of 4.","An atypical pigment network consists of irregular meshes and thickened lines.","Irregular streaks are unevenly distributed radial lines or pseudopods.","Irregular dots and globules have varied size and uneven distribution.","The presence of these features, even if subtle, is sufficient to trigger the 7-point checklist’s melanoma suspicion threshold.","The absence of blue-whitish veil, vascular structures, pigmentation, and regression structures does not reduce the score, as these were scored as absent and do not contribute points."]
